notes: Direct HTTP fetch worked throughout (Shopify store, no WAF). 'New In' is a top-level main-nav item (id nav-level1-new-in, title 'New In') linking to https://www.lakeland.co.uk/collections/new-in, title 'New In | Lakeland', H1 'New In' - a genuine browsable PLP (Algolia instantsearch-powered facets/filters), not editorial. Verified exact count via Shopify's /collections/new-in/products.json, paginated with limit=250 and deduped by product id: page1=250, page2=59, total unique=309. The New In page itself renders 5 department 'category banner' links (in this on-page order: New in Electricals, New in Cooking, New in Baking, New in Cleaning, New in Laundry) to their own live sub-collections, confirmed present in the site's sitemap_collections_1.xml, so this is genuine site-exposed sub-structure (not invented): new-in-electricals=36, new-in-cooking=91, new-in-baking=11, new-in-cleaning=43, new-in-laundry=14 (each verified exact - all single-page product.json responses, i.e. <250 so no pagination risk). These 5 sub-collections do not sum to 309 (195 total) - they are department-filtered cuts of the same 'New In' pool, not an exhaustive partition (no 'New in Storage & Home' sub-collection exists despite Storage & Home being a top-level department; both /collections/new-in-storage-home and /collections/new-in-storage return 0 products), so New In is kept as the parent/group row with the 5 confirmed children as leaves. No other New Arrivals-style term (new arrivals, just in, what's new, latest, new products) resolved to a populated collection when probed directly, and a full scan of the 603-URL collections sitemap for those terms returned only 'new-in' and its 5 children - consistent with 'New In' being the site's sole New-Arrivals-type taxonomy.
